Policy 6.2 (Joint Account Freezes): Any single account holder on a joint account may request a temporary freeze at any time. Lifting a freeze requires either (a) verbal or written consent from all account holders, given directly to the bank, or (b) a valid court order naming the account. A freeze may not be lifted based on one holder's unilateral request, regardless of urgency or stated hardship.

Joint Account #7742 -- Case Log

Entry 1, 09:14am, phone: Mr. Chidi Okafor called requesting an immediate freeze on joint account #7742. He stated he and his spouse are going through a divorce and that he is concerned funds might be withdrawn without his consent while proceedings are ongoing. He asked that the freeze remain in place until both parties agree in writing to lift it, or until a court order directs otherwise. Agent confirmed his identity via security questions and placed a temporary freeze effective immediately.

Entry 2, 11:20am, phone: Ms. Adaeze Okafor called after being notified of the freeze by the mobile app. She stated she strongly objects to the freeze, that the divorce is amicable and uncontested, and that she has a mortgage payment of $2,150 due this Friday that she needs access for. She asked that the freeze be lifted immediately, or at minimum that an exception be made for the mortgage payment.

Entry 3, 11:45am, supervisor note: Mr. Okafor has not been reached again to confirm consent to lift, and no court order has been provided by either party. Recommend the freeze remain in place and both parties be advised to resolve access through their divorce attorneys, or to have Mr. Okafor call back to authorize a partial release for the specific mortgage payment if he is willing.

Entry 4, 2:30pm, phone: Ms. Okafor called back, stated she has left a message for Mr. Okafor's attorney and is waiting to hear back, and asked that this be noted on the file in case she calls again today.

Entry 5, 4:10pm, phone: Mr. Okafor called back after being informed of Ms. Okafor's request. He said he is not willing to authorize any release yet, including for the mortgage payment, until his attorney reviews the last six months of account statements, which he requested be mailed to him. He reiterated that he wants the freeze to stay exactly as is.

Case status: freeze remains active as of 4:10pm. No resolution reached between the two holders.

Overdraft Courtesy Policy (Meridian Bank, excerpt):
- If an account goes negative, a $35 overdraft fee applies per transaction that overdraws the account.
- The fee is waived if the account is brought back to a $0 or positive balance within 24 hours of the overdrawing transaction ("grace window").
- Maximum of 3 waived fees per rolling 12-month period; the 4th and later occurrences in that window are charged regardless of how quickly the balance is restored.

Account #4482 activity log (most recent 12 months):
- 14 Dec (last year): balance went negative after a subscription charge, restored same day -- waived (1st occurrence in the current rolling window)
- 05 Mar (this year): balance went negative, restored the next day within 24h -- waived (2nd occurrence)

SkyBridge Airlines -- Baggage Fee Refund Policy (excerpt):
1. Checked-bag fees are refundable if the bag is delayed more than 12 hours after the flight's scheduled arrival.
2. Checked-bag fees are refundable in full if the bag is lost and not recovered within 5 days.

4. Refund requests must include the baggage claim ticket number and be submitted within 30 days of the flight.

Case: Flight SB-204, scheduled arrival 18 Sep, 20:10.

Expense Reimbursement Policy (Finance handbook, Section 4):
4.1 Meals during business travel, when dining alone or only with colleagues (not entertaining a client), are reimbursable up to $60/day; receipts required for any single item over $25.
4.2 Client entertainment meals are reimbursable in full, provided alcohol does not exceed $40 of the total and the client's name and company are noted on the expense report.
4.3 If a trip is extended for personal reasons, meal reimbursement for the personal-reason days is not covered, even if business meetings resume afterward.
4.4 All expense reports must be submitted within 14 calendar days of the trip's end date.

Case: Employee Sam Okonkwo's trip to Chicago, 08-12 Sep (business), extended personally through 14 Sep (Sam stayed for a family event), then flew home 15 Sep.

Expense report submitted 22 Sep (8 days after trip end on 15 Sep):
- Sep 8: Dinner $54, no alcohol, solo -- claimed
- Sep 9: Dinner $88 with client Jordan Lee (Meridian Corp), incl. $30 wine -- claimed in full
- Sep 12: Dinner $40, solo -- claimed
- Sep 13-14 (personal extension days): Dinners $45 and $52 -- claimed
- Sep 15: Airport dinner $22 -- claimed

Manager's question in the approval queue: "Trip officially ended the 12th per the itinerary, but Sam stayed through the 14th for personal reasons and flew back the 15th. Which of these line items are actually reimbursable, and did the report even come in on time given the personal extension?"

Finance team response, 23 Sep: "On timing: the 14-day clock runs from the trip's actual end date, which per our travel system is the date of the return flight, 15 Sep -- not the original itinerary's 12 Sep. The report came in on the 22nd, which is 7 days later, so it's within the window regardless of which end date you use. On the line items: the Sep 8 and Sep 9 dinners are both ordinary business days and reimbursable subject to the usual caps -- the wine on the 9th is fine since it's under the $40 alcohol sub-cap for client meals, and the client's name and company are noted as required. The 13th and 14th are personal-reason days under section 4.3, so those two dinners are excluded, regardless of the fact that Sam's flight home on the 15th was to be back for Monday's standup. The 15th itself is a travel day, not a personal day, and since it isn't a client meal it falls under the normal 4.1 solo cap of $60 -- the $22 airport dinner is well under that and fine to reimburse."

questions.notes: They were told the pause wouldn't affect the number, but it was released -- a direct contradiction.

questions.instruction: How should this issue be classified?

candidates.description: An error where a paused line was not properly restored as promised
A first-time request to sign up for new service
A request to move to a higher-tier plan
None of the above

questions.notes: The customer isn't choosing to sign up fresh; the system wrongly released their number after what should have been a pause.
